glossary.Large bowel obstruction: Blockage of the colon causing distension, vomiting, constipation and no flatus.
glossary.Benign: Not cancerous and does not spread.
glossary.Pre-malignant: Not yet cancer but able to become cancer.
glossary.Polyps: Small growths projecting from the bowel lining.
glossary.IBD: Inflammatory bowel disease: Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis.
glossary.External beam radiotherapy: Radiation aimed at a tumour from a machine outside the body.
glossary.Caecal: Relating to the caecum, the first pouch of the large bowel in the right iliac fossa.
glossary.Iron-deficiency anaemia: Low haemoglobin from lack of iron, often from slow blood loss.
glossary.RIF: Right iliac fossa: the lower right part of the abdomen.
glossary.LIF: Left iliac fossa: the lower left part of the abdomen.
glossary.Sigmoid: The S-shaped last part of the colon before the rectum.
glossary.Colicky pain: Pain that comes and goes in waves, typical of a blocked hollow organ.
glossary.Lipomas: Benign fatty lumps under the skin.
glossary.Supernumerary teeth: Extra teeth beyond the normal number.
glossary.Osteomas: Benign bony growths, often on the skull or jaw.
glossary.Epidermoid cysts: Benign skin cysts filled with keratin.
glossary.AD: Autosomal dominant: one faulty copy of the gene is enough to cause the condition.
glossary.Endometrial: Relating to the lining of the womb.
glossary.Sebaceous gland: Skin gland that produces oily sebum.
glossary.Metastases: Secondary tumours that have spread from the original cancer.
glossary.Biopsy: A small tissue sample taken for examination under the microscope.
glossary.Direct visualisation: Looking at the bowel lining directly with a camera.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count, which shows anaemia.
glossary.LFTs: Liver function tests, which may be deranged by liver metastases.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood tests of kidney function.
glossary.MRI pelvis: Magnetic resonance scan of the pelvis, used to stage rectal cancer.
glossary.CT CAP: CT scan of the chest, abdomen and pelvis, used to look for spread.
glossary.Tumour marker: A blood substance made by a cancer, used to track response and recurrence.
glossary.Endoscopic: Done through a camera passed into the gut.
glossary.Primary anastomosis: Joining the bowel ends back together in the same operation.
glossary.Splenic flexure: The bend of the colon near the spleen, between transverse and descending colon.
glossary.High anterior resection: Removal of the sigmoid colon and upper rectum with a join.
glossary.Anal verge: The outer edge of the anus, used as a landmark for rectal tumour height.
glossary.Oncology: The specialty that treats cancer with drugs and radiotherapy.
glossary.Palliative: Aimed at relieving symptoms rather than curing.
glossary.Stenting: Placing a tube across a narrowed bowel to keep it open.
glossary.Perforation: A hole through the bowel wall, leaking contents into the abdomen.
glossary.Diverticulitis: Inflammation or infection of small pouches in the colon wall.
glossary.Distension: Swelling of the abdomen from gas or fluid.
glossary.Flatus: Wind passed from the back passage.
glossary.Delirium: Acute confusion, often from infection or illness.
glossary.Sepsis: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by the body's response to infection.
glossary.Peritonitic: Showing peritonitis: a rigid, very tender abdomen from inflamed peritoneum.
glossary.Exploratory laparotomy: Opening the abdomen surgically to find and treat a problem.
glossary.Tumour suppressor gene: A gene that normally stops cells dividing out of control.
glossary.Sporadic: Occurring by chance rather than inherited.
glossary.Germline: Present in every cell from birth, so it can be inherited.
glossary.MSH6: One of the DNA mismatch repair genes mutated in Lynch syndrome.
glossary.PMS2: One of the DNA mismatch repair genes mutated in Lynch syndrome.
glossary.Circumferentially: Growing all the way around the bowel wall.
glossary.Portal venous drainage: Blood from the gut drains via the portal vein to the liver, so cancer spreads there first.
glossary.Mucosa: The inner lining of the bowel.
